likely_cause.reasoning: The domain is still registered through the business's own registrar account with its own nameserver pair and is paid until 1 August 2028, so it has not lapsed, been parked or been re-registered by anyone else. The live page is the genuine Bussel site (its own brokers, listings and deal news), so the site was not replaced. What differs is content injected into it: a hidden off-canvas block of Binomo/gambling, passport and Russian retail spam with four outbound links, plus a horse emoji added to the tab title. The Wayback snapshot of 4 August 2026 is clean, and a plain-HTML fetch of the same URL today is clean, while a real Chrome navigation today carries the spam — consistent with an injection that is served selectively. Inference: injected SEO spam on the business's own site, not a domain loss; the selective serving cannot be confirmed without server access.

fix_steps.step: Change the hosting/IIS, FTP, database, /login.asp admin and mailbox passwords and enable two-factor where offered. Leave the domain registration where it is: it is paid to 2028 and locked.

Ask the host for access/FTP logs around the last template change to find the entry point, patch it (outdated component, weak FTP or admin password) and keep IIS and the ASP stack updated.
Check Google Search Console for Security Issues and Manual Actions on bussel.com, request a review once the spam is gone, and set up a weekly alert on outbound links and the page title.
fix_steps.who: Developer, then owner for the weekly check

fix_steps.step: Fix the contact path while the developer is in: /contact-us/ returns a bare 404 and the contact page's only form is the CRM login. Point /contact-us/ at the directory page and add a public enquiry route.

after_fix.opportunity: Add a public enquiry/requirement form (property type, size, location, timeline) and click-to-call on the phone number, so a tenant or landlord can reach the right broker without the CRM login or copying a number by hand.

severity_reason: Customers see a normal, working brokerage site and the domain is safe and paid until 2028, so there is no outage. The damage is to search visibility and trust: the site serves hidden gambling, passport and Russian-retail links to browsers, its page title is altered, and its /contact-us/ URL returns a 404.
audit_md:
# Website Health Check: Bussel Realty Corp

**What we saw on 13 November 2026**

- bussel.com is registered through GoDaddy in the company's own account, paid until 1 August 2028 with registrar locks on, so it has not lapsed or changed hands.
- The site loads normally in Chrome — logo, 732-287-3777, property search, listings, deal news — but the home page also carries a hidden off-screen block of Vietnamese, Hebrew and Russian spam linking to vietnam-millionaire.me, portuguese-passport.online, top10binary.ru and top10shops.ru, and the tab title is prefixed with a horse emoji.
- A plain text fetch of that same page returns clean HTML, so the spam is served only some of the time.
- Google's "Bussel Realty Corporation" profile (4.5, 2 Ethel Rd #202a, Edison NJ 08817) lists bussel.com, so that is where customers are sent; bussel.com/contact-us/ returns a bare 404.

**What it means for customers**

Visitors see a normal, working site; the injected text sits out of view. Search engines can still read it, and spam links like these can cost rankings or bring a security warning.

**How to fix it**

1. Change hosting, FTP, database and staff-login passwords and add two-factor; leave the domain registration alone (1–2 hours).
2. Diff the home page against the clean Wayback copy of 4 August 2026, then strip the injected block from the templates and includes (3–6 hours).
3. Have the host trace the entry point in the access logs and patch it (2–4 hours).
4. Check Search Console for security issues, request a review, add weekly page monitoring (1–2 hours).
5. Repair /contact-us/ and add a public enquiry route (2–4 hours).

**After the fix**

Add click-to-call on 732-287-3777 and a short requirement form, so a tenant or landlord reaches a broker in one tap.

Prepared from publicly available information on 13 November 2026. We did not log in to or change anything.

Subject: Something on bussel.com you might not be able to see

We have screenshots of the desktop and phone view alongside the page code, and I am happy to send them over so your developer can check whether anything else was touched. It is a contained, specific job — removing the injected block and closing the way it got in — and I can walk you through what we saw in ten minutes.

"I was on your website this morning and spotted hidden spam links baked into the home page that you would never see as a visitor — can I show you the screenshots?"

**Sources**

**Open questions**

- Who holds the registrar (GoDaddy) and hosting/IIS logins, and when were those passwords last changed?
- Who builds and maintains the classic ASP site — in-house, a web firm, or the host?
